sentences.text: Tidal current is the horizontal flow of water caused by the tide.
A current is named for the direction it flows toward, called its set, while wind is named for the direction it comes from.
So a north wind blows toward the south, but a north-setting current flows toward the north.
That difference shows up on the exam.
Flood current flows toward land, ebb away from it, and slack water is the brief period between.
In rivers and inlets currents reverse direction, while offshore they may be rotary, turning steadily around the compass.
Slack water often doesn’t coincide with high or low tide, especially in inlets, so never assume one from the other.
